s: What was the rent ceiling generally contemplated under tenancy reform?
o: One-half to two-thirds of the produce
One-tenth to one-twentieth of the produce
One-third to one-half of the produce
One-fourth to one-sixth of the produce
x: Tenancy reform sought to regulate rent by limiting it to approximately one-fourth to one-sixth of the produce.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Land consolidation is associated with land reform.
Tenancy reform concerns rent, tenure and ownership.
Land ceiling refers to the minimum legal holding permitted.
Abolition of intermediaries aims to remove middlemen.
x: Option C is incorrect: a land ceiling is the maximum land one may legally hold, not the minimum. Surplus above it is redistributed.

s:
Consider the following statements about land reforms in India:
1. Land reforms contribute to the reduction of inequality.
2. Land ceiling facilitates the redistribution of surplus land.
3. Land ceiling fixes the maximum rent payable by tenants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Land reforms reduce inequality because ceilings free surplus land for the landless; rent regulation is part of tenancy reform, not the ceiling, so 3 is wrong.

s: What share of the cultivable area did land ceiling laws in India redistribute?
x: Despite two rounds of ceiling laws (1950s and early 1970s), less than 2% of cultivable area was redistributed.

s: Which of the following was an important reason for the limited redistribution achieved through land ceiling laws?
o: Absence of any ceiling legislation in the States
Exemptions for plantations, orchards and mechanised farms
Automatic transfer of all surplus land to corporations
x: Exemptions for plantations, orchards and mechanised farms reduced the amount of land available for redistribution.

s: The 1972 national guidelines on land ceiling adopted which unit for fixing the ceiling?
x: Pre-1972 laws used the individual as the unit, encouraging benami transfers; the 1972 guidelines shifted to the family.

s: What was the land ceiling for dry land under the 1972 national guidelines?
x: The guidelines set 10-18 acres for two-crop irrigated land, 27 for single-crop and 54 for dry land.

s: Ceiling laws before 1972 took the individual as the unit. What did this encourage?
x: The individual unit fuelled benami transfers to relatives; the 1972 guidelines shifted to the family unit.

s: Through which of the following did tenancy reforms in India largely fail?
x: Tenancy reform was defeated by so-called voluntary surrenders and evictions.

s: Indira Prabha, a scheme to develop barren lands allotted to the landless poor, was introduced by which Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Indira Prabha was introduced by Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy to develop barren lands given to landless poor farmers.

s: With which subject did the Koneru Ranga Rao Committee mainly deal?
x: It was a Land Committee on land-related problems in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Under whose chairmanship was the National Council for Land Reforms constituted in 2008?
x: The National Council for Land Reforms was constituted in 2008 under the Prime Minister.

s: Which government set up the Koneru Ranga Rao Committee (2006)?
x: The AP Land Committee of 2006 was set up by the Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy government.

s: Who prepared the Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016?
x: The Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was prepared by NITI Aayog, with inputs associated with the T. Haque Committee.

s: Which was the first State to implement the Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016?
x: Uttarakhand, not Andhra Pradesh, was the first State to implement the Model Act (APPSC 2018 key).

s: Who headed the committee that drafted the Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016?
x: NITI Aayog's T. Haque committee prepared the Model Act.

s:
Consider the following statements about Operation Barga:
1. It was carried out in West Bengal under the Left Front government.
2. Recorded bargadars got heritable rights.
3. Recorded bargadars were entitled to 25% of the produce.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: Operation Barga was a West Bengal Left Front programme. Statement 2 is correct: recorded bargadars got heritable rights. Statement 3 is wrong: their share was 75% of the produce, not 25%. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 include the wrong share.

s: Whose names was Operation Barga mainly meant to record?
x: Operation Barga recorded the names of sharecroppers, known as bargadars, and thereby strengthened their rights.

s: What share of the produce did recorded bargadars get under Operation Barga?
x: Bargadars got heritable rights and a 75% share of the produce.

s: In which year was Operation Barga launched in West Bengal?
x: Operation Barga began in 1978 under the Left Front; the Bengal Land Holding Revenue Act came in 1979.

s: Consolidation of holdings achieved comparatively greater success in which group of regions?
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
x: Consolidation succeeded in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, while it made little progress in southern and eastern States.

s: What did the Kumarappa Committee, 1949 recommend?
x: The Kumarappa Committee recommended cooperative farming in 1949.

s: What share of their land did the Bhoodan movement ask landowners to donate?
x: Vinoba Bhave appealed for 1/6th of land; over 40 lakh acres were pledged.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of joint cooperative farming?
o: Produce is shared according to land contributed
Produce is shared according to labour contributed
Membership is compulsory for all landowners
x: In joint cooperative farming land is pooled voluntarily and produce is shared by land and labour put in; membership is not compulsory.

s: Under joint cooperative farming, how is the produce shared among members?
o: According to the land and labour contributed
Wholly by the State procurement agency
Only by the number of family members
x: Members pool land voluntarily and share the produce according to the land and labour each contributed.

s: Where did Acharya Vinoba Bhave start the Bhoodan movement on 18 April 1951?
x: Bhoodan began at Pochampally in Nalgonda (now Telangana) on 18 April 1951, during the Telangana armed struggle.

s: Which session of the Congress, in 1959, made cooperative farming a party goal?
x: The Nagpur Resolution (1959) made cooperative farming a goal, following the Kumarappa Committee (1949); it later failed.

s: Which movement was called the 'Bloodless Revolution'?
x: Vinoba Bhave's Bhoodan movement (1951), which asked for 1/6th of land as gift and led to Gramdan, was called the Bloodless Revolution.

s: Clause (h), relating to rent and tenancy rights in Article 323B, was added by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: Clause (h) concerning rent and tenancy rights was added to Article 323B by the 75th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1993.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Articles 31A and 31B and added the Ninth Schedule?
x: The First Amendment Act of 1951 inserted Articles 31A and 31B and created the Ninth Schedule in the context of land-reform protection.

s: The meaning of which term was widened by the Seventeenth Amendment Act, 1964?
x: The 17th Amendment widened 'estate'; Article 31C came later through the 25th Amendment.

s: In I.R. Coelho, the Supreme Court held that Ninth Schedule laws added after which date are open to Basic Structure review?
x: Laws added after 24 April 1973, the date of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment, can be reviewed against the Basic Structure.

s: Which of the following Amendment–provision pairs is correctly matched?
x: The 25th Amendment inserted Article 31C; the 1st inserted 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule; the 75th added 323B(h).

s: Under the 17th Amendment (1964), at what rate must compensation be paid for acquiring land under personal cultivation within the ceiling?
x: Such land could be acquired only at market value; the Amendment was challenged in Golaknath (1967).

s: Which Constitutional Amendment widened Article 31A to cover zamindari abolition, planning and mineral control?
x: The 4th Amendment (1955) restated Article 31(2) and widened Article 31A.

s: In which case was the Seventeenth Amendment (1964) challenged?
o: Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar
I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
x: The 17th Amendment, which widened 'estate', was challenged in Golaknath (1967).

s: After which case was the First Amendment (1951) brought, inserting Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule?
o: Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
x: The 1st Amendment (1951) followed the Kameshwar Singh v. Bihar case and protected land reform laws.

s: Which was the first Act for the abolition of intermediaries?
o: Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948
x: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 was the first intermediary-abolition Act.

s: Which committee recommended the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act in the Andhra area?
x: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act was recommended by the Prakasam Committee in 1938.

s: What did jagirs and Sarf-e-khas lands become after the Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949?
x: Following the Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949, jagirs and Sarf-e-khas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after Police Action.

s: Under the Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy Act, 1950, in how many instalments could a protected tenant become owner by paying 60% of the market price?
x: Ownership was on paying 60% of the market price in 20 instalments, not 10.

s: What was the maximum rent fixed for wet land under the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956?
x: The Act (on the Subba Rao Committee's advice) capped rent at 30% for wet land and 25% for dry land.

s: On whose recommendations was the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956 based?
x: The Subba Rao Committee led to the 1956 Act; the Prakasam Committee (1938) related to estate abolition.

s: Under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Basic unit of ceiling – family of five
Each extra family member – one-fifth of the ceiling added
Lands of husband and wife – treated as separate units
x: The husband's and wife's lands are clubbed together, not treated as separate units.

s: Persons who grab which lands are punished under the AP Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982?
o: Only forest land outside municipal limits
x: The Act punishes grabbers of government lands and lands belonging to weaker sections.

s: On which date did the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 come into force?
x: Introduced under CM P.V. Narasimha Rao and placed in the Ninth Schedule, the Act came into force on 1 January 1975.

s: What does the AP Assigned Lands (Prohibition of Transfers) Act, 1977 provide for land assigned to the landless poor?
o: Can be mortgaged only to private moneylenders
Can be freely sold after five years
x: The Act prohibits the sale or transfer of land assigned to landless poor persons.

s: What were the standard ceiling limits under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973?
x: Under the AP Ceiling Act, 1973, the ceiling was 10–27 acres for wet land and 35–54 acres for dry land.

s: Who headed a Land Tribunal under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973?
x: The Land Tribunal was headed by the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO).

s: The Srikakulam Naxalite unrest and the 1966-69 droughts pushed which development in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The second phase of land reforms
x: The Srikakulam unrest and the 1966-69 droughts pushed Phase II of land reforms in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Under the AP Ceiling Act, 1973, benami transfers made after which date are ignored?
x: Benami transfers after 30 January 1970 are disregarded under the 1973 Act.

s: In Phase II of AP land ceiling, about 20 lakh acres were estimated surplus, but only about how much was taken over?
x: Only about 5 lakh acres were taken over against an estimated 20 lakh acres of surplus.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the unit under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973?
o: The unit is a family of five
Husband's and wife's land is clubbed
Each major son is a separate unit
The unit is the individual landholder
x: The 1973 Act takes a family of 5 as the unit; the individual unit was used by the 1961 Act.

s: Under which Chief Minister was the Bill for the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 brought?
x: The 1973 Ceiling Bill was brought under CM P.V. Narasimha Rao; the Act was put in the Ninth Schedule and came into force on 1 January 1975.

s: What was the unit of ceiling under the Andhra Pradesh Ceiling Act, 1961?
x: The 1961 Act took the individual as unit (27-324 acres); the 1973 Act moved to a family of five.

s: On what does the NCAER Land Records and Services Index (N-LRSI) mainly evaluate States?
o: Digitisation and quality of land records
x: NCAER’s Land Records and Services Index grades States on the digitisation and quality of their land records.

s: Karnataka's Bhoomi project, launched in 2000, was a pioneer of what?
o: Computerised Records of Rights, Tenancy and Crops (RTCs)
x: Bhoomi (2000) pioneered computerised RTCs; Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN) is a DILRMP feature, not Bhoomi's.

s: When did Andhra Pradesh's land resurvey under Jagananna Saswatha Bhu Hakku and Bhu Raksha begin?
x: The resurvey began in December 2020, using drones, CORS and GIS, and covers 6,901 villages and 81 lakh parcels.

s: Bhu Bharathi, associated with the computerisation of land records in the erstwhile united Andhra Pradesh, was initiated in which year?
x: Bhu Bharathi was initiated in 1992 as a computerisation initiative for land records in the erstwhile united Andhra Pradesh.

s: What do the QR-coded pattadar passbooks issued in Andhra Pradesh from January 2026 carry?
x: The new passbooks carry the State emblem; 36 lakh were issued, with 56 lakh more planned by March 2027.

s: What is CARD in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Drone survey programme for abadi areas
Registration system offering anywhere registration and auto-mutation
Property card scheme of the Panchayati Raj Ministry
x: CARD is a registration system offering anywhere registration, auto-mutation and registration at Grama Sachivalayams; it is not a court.

s: In the NCAER Land Records and Services Index, Andhra Pradesh's rank improved from 10th in 2020 to which rank in 2021?
x: AP rose from 10th (2020) to 6th (2021) in N-LRSI; Madhya Pradesh was at the top.

s: Which State topped the NCAER Land Records and Services Index (N-LRSI)?
x: Madhya Pradesh was at the top of N-LRSI, while AP ranked 6th in 2021.

s: Bhu Bharathi, the land-records computerisation project of united Andhra Pradesh, was piloted in which district?
x: Bhu Bharathi (1992) was piloted in Nizamabad.

s: Andhra Pradesh's Mee Bhoomi-Blockchain pilot, launched on 24 July 2026, covers how many mandals?
x: The Mee Bhoomi-Blockchain pilot began on 24 July 2026 in 7 mandals.

s: What is the name of Andhra Pradesh's digitised land records platform?
x: Webland is AP's digitised land records platform; Bhoomi is Karnataka's and Dharani is Telangana's.

s: Andhra Pradesh's land resurvey (from December 2020) has covered how many villages?
x: The AP resurvey using drones, CORS and GIS covered 6,901 villages and 81 lakh parcels.

s: What is the full form of SVAMITVA?
o: Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas
Systematic Valuation and Mapping of Inhabited Technology Villages and Areas
Survey of Village Assets and Mapping through Integrated Technology in Village Areas
State Verification and Mapping of Titles in Village Agricultural Areas
x: SVAMITVA expands to Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas.

s: SVAMITVA was launched on which occasion and date?
x: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020, the occasion of National Panchayati Raj Day. Its pilot was conducted in 2020 and it was taken nationwide in 2021.

s: Which organisation is the implementing agency for SVAMITVA and which organisation provides its technology support?
o: NCAER and Department of Land Resources, respectively
Department of Land Resources and State Election Commissions, respectively
Survey of India and NICSI, respectively
NICSI and Survey of India, respectively
x: The Survey of India is the implementing agency for SVAMITVA, while NICSI provides technology support.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about SVAMITVA?
o: Its Property Cards can be accessed through DigiLocker
Its Property Cards function as Records of Rights
Agricultural land is covered under its property-card survey
x: SVAMITVA covers rural abadi areas, not agricultural land.

s: SVAMITVA scheme is implemented under which Ministry, and of what type of scheme is it?
o: Ministry of Mines; Centrally Sponsored Scheme
Ministry of Panchayati Raj; Central Sector Scheme
Ministry of Rural Development; Centrally Sponsored Scheme
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Central Sector Scheme
x: SVAMITVA belongs to the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and is a Central Sector scheme. The Ministry of Mines is a common trap; Rural Development handles DILRMP's Department of Land Resources, and Agriculture has no role in it.

s: SVAMITVA targets how many villages?
x: The target is 6.62 lakh villages at Rs 566.23 crore; over 2.76 crore property cards have been prepared.

s:
Consider the following statements about SVAMITVA:
1. Its output is Property Cards for village households.
2. It uses drone surveys.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Mines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: SVAMITVA issues Property Cards (2.76 crore+) through drone surveys; it is under the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, not Mines.

s: Which kind of land do SVAMITVA surveys cover?
x: SVAMITVA covers abadi areas only, not agricultural land.

s: About how many SVAMITVA Property Cards have been prepared so far?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (3.06 crore); it is added as option 5.
the old figure was 2.76 crore property cards — now 3.06 crore (Rocket CA 2026-01 p.153, January 2026)
SVAMITVA had prepared 3.06 crore property cards in 1.86 lakh villages by January 2026 (earlier figure 2.76 crore).

s: What is ULPIN, also called Bhu-Aadhaar?
o: 12-digit numeric ID based on the owner's Aadhaar number
14-digit alphanumeric ID generated from the geo-coordinates of a parcel's vertices
14-digit numeric ID based on the village survey number
16-digit alphanumeric ID issued for agricultural loans
x: ULPIN (Unique Land Parcel Identification Number) is a 14-digit alphanumeric ID derived from the geo-coordinates of a parcel's vertices.

s: What is the National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS)?
o: A common, configurable registration application for sub-registrars and citizens under DILRMP
A drone-based village-survey platform operated exclusively by Survey of India
A ranking system for assessing the quality of State land records
A land-dispute tribunal established under the Model Conclusive Land Titling Act
x: The National Generic Document Registration System is the ‘One Nation One Registration Software’ under DILRMP, serving sub-registrars and citizens through a common configurable application.

s: By what name is the National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS) known?
x: NGDRS is 'One Nation One Registration Software' under DILRMP, a common application for sub-registrars and citizens, not an index.

s: Under the National Digital Land Initiative (Land Stack), what is assigned to every land parcel?
x: Land Stack is a cloud-based GIS framework that assigns a Bhu-Aadhaar to every parcel.

s: The tenure of DILRMP was extended up to which period, along with which two new components?
o: 2025-26; consent-based Aadhaar seeding of land records and computerisation of revenue courts
x: The programme was extended from 2021-22 to 2025-26. Consent-based Aadhaar seeding of land records and computerisation of revenue courts were added as new components.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the phases of DILRMP 3.0 is correctly matched?
o: Phase 3 – Digitisation, resurvey and cadastral maps
Phase 2 – ULPIN, NGDRS and e-Court integration
x: Phase 2 (2016-26) added ULPIN, NGDRS, multilingual records and e-Court integration; Phase 1 covered digitisation and resurvey, and Phase 3 the GIS-based Land Stack.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the land-record modernisation programme (DILRMP)?
o: It became a Central Sector Scheme in 2016
x: The programme began as NLRMP in 2008 and became a Central Sector Scheme in 2016; ULPIN came in Phase 2 (2016-26), not Phase 1.

s: The National Land Records Modernisation Programme (NLRMP), launched in 2008, was formed by merging which two earlier schemes?
o: Computerisation of Land Records (CLR) and Strengthening of Revenue Administration and Updating of Land Records (SRA&ULR)
National Generic Document Registration System and ULPIN
x: NLRMP (2008) merged CLR and SRA&ULR. SVAMITVA (2020) and NAKSHA are later schemes; NGDRS and ULPIN are DILRMP tools; Bhoomi (Karnataka) and Bhu Bharathi (AP) are State projects.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP)?
o: It has been a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding since 1 April 2016
It continues to be a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with cost-sharing by States
Digitisation of cadastral maps is one of its components
x: DILRMP was centrally sponsored only before 2016; since 1 April 2016 it is a Central Sector Scheme.

s: Under DILRMP, about what share of Records of Rights have been digitised?
x: RoR digitisation is 99.8%; cadastral maps are 97.24% digitised and 95.73% of SROs computerised.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of DILRMP?
o: Issue of Property Cards for abadi areas
x: Property Cards for abadi areas are the output of SVAMITVA; record rooms, digitised cadastral maps and computerised registration are DILRMP components.

s: Since 1 April 2016, how has DILRMP been funded?
o: Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding
x: From 1 April 2016 DILRMP is a Central Sector scheme with 100% central funding; earlier it was centrally sponsored.

s: Under DILRMP, which column has been made mandatory in the Record of Rights?
x: DILRMP made a gender column mandatory in the Record of Rights, along with consent-based Aadhaar seeding.

s: Why are clear land titles economically significant?
o: abolish the need for land registration
turn land into collateral and help reduce litigation
guarantee that no land dispute ever arises
x: Clear titles let land be used as collateral and can reduce litigation; they do not abolish registration or end every dispute.

s: Which of the following is true under the conclusive system of land titling?
o: Title may be challenged through earlier deeds
The State guarantees the title once issued
x: In the conclusive system the State guarantees title; in the presumptive system registration only records a transaction and title can be challenged.

s: Under the presumptive system of land titling followed at present, what does registration of a deed do?
o: Only records a transaction, and the title can be challenged
Makes the State guarantor of the title
x: In presumptive titling registration only records a transaction and the title can be challenged; State guarantee and a single title register belong to conclusive titling.

s: A single title register replacing separate registration, survey and revenue records is a feature of which system?
x: Conclusive titling keeps a single title register; under presumptive titling registration, survey and revenue records are kept separately.

s: What is the position on adoption of the NITI Aayog Model Conclusive Land Titling Act, 2020 by States?
o: A matter of each State's choice
Compulsory for States receiving DILRMP funds
x: It is a model framework; adoption is left to the States. It aims to reduce disputes, ease credit and lower transaction costs.

s: In its ruling of 1 January 2026, what did the Supreme Court hold registration of a transfer deed to be?
o: valid only after proof of mutation
conclusive proof of title in every case
x: The Court held that registration of a transfer deed is distinct from title and did not uphold Bihar's rule requiring mandatory proof of mutation.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Land Titling Act, under which the State acts as guarantor of titles, sought to move the State from which system to which?
x: The Act sought a shift from presumptive to conclusive titling, with the State as guarantor of land titles.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Land Titling Act, 2022 repealed?
x: The AP Land Titling Act, 2022 (Act 27 of 2023) was repealed in 2024 by Act 11 of 2024.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Land Titling Act, 2022 was criticised for limiting land disputes to which forum?
x: The Act was criticised for limiting disputes to the High Court and was repealed in 2024.

s: To which of the following does NABARD provide refinance?
o: Only RRBs and State Cooperative Banks
Only Scheduled Commercial Banks and RRBs
SCBs, RRBs, State Land Development Banks and State Cooperative Banks
x: All four – scheduled commercial banks, RRBs, State Land Development Banks and State Cooperative Banks – get NABARD refinance.

s:
Consider the following about NABARD:
1. The RBI sold its stake in NABARD in 2019.
2. NABARD is now fully owned by the Government of India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The RBI sold its stake in 2019, after which NABARD became fully owned by the Government of India.

s: From which source is the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) funded?
o: Deposits of banks that fall short of PSL targets
x: RIDF uses banks' PSL shortfall deposits and lends to States for rural roads, bridges and irrigation.

s: What is the corpus of the Warehouse Infrastructure Fund (2013-14) managed by NABARD?
x: The WIF is Rs 5,000 crore; LTIF (Rs 1,441 crore) and the Food Processing Fund (Rs 2,000 crore) are other NABARD funds.

s: During which Five Year Plan was NABARD, the apex bank for agricultural refinance, established?
x: NABARD was set up in 1982, during the Sixth Plan.

s: Why is NABARD regarded as the apex agricultural and rural finance institution?
o: Lends directly to farmers through Kisan Credit Cards
Refinances the banks that lend in rural areas
Is the main lender to MSMEs
x: NABARD's main job is refinancing the banks that lend in rural areas; it does not lend to farmers directly, and SIDBI is the MSME lender.

s: Where is the headquarters of NABARD?
x: NABARD is headquartered in Mumbai.

s: In which year did Parliament pass the NABARD Act?
x: The NABARD Act was passed in 1981 (Act 61 of 1981); NABARD was established on 12 July 1982.

s: Which of the following was NOT merged into NABARD at its formation?
x: NABARD took over RBI's ACD, the RPCC and ARDC; IFCI was not merged.

s: Which of the following was taken over by NABARD at its inception?
x: NABARD took over the ARDC, along with the RBI's Agricultural Credit Department and Rural Planning and Credit Cell; IFCI was not merged.

s: What is the full form of RIDF, the fund administered by NABARD?
x: RIDF is the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund; NABARD lends from it to States for rural roads, bridges and irrigation.

s: On which date was NABARD established?
x: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 under the NABARD Act, 1981.

s:
Consider the following statements about NABARD:
1. It was established on 12 July 1982.
2. It was established during the Fifth Five Year Plan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982, during the Sixth Five Year Plan, not the Fifth.

s: In which year did NABARD set up the ₹2,000 crore Food Processing Fund?
x: The Food Processing Fund of ₹2,000 crore came in 2014-15; the Warehouse Infrastructure Fund came in 2013-14.

s: Into which document do NABARD's district-level Potential Linked Credit Plans (PLPs) roll up?
x: District PLPs roll up into NABARD's State Focus Paper, which is the base for the State's Annual Credit Plan.

s: What is the size of NABARD's credit plan for Andhra Pradesh for 2026-27?
x: The AP 2026-27 plan is Rs 5.11 lakh crore (about 20% more), with agriculture at Rs 2.55 lakh crore and crop loans Rs 1.66 lakh crore.

s: The State Focus Paper prepared by NABARD forms the base of which plan?
o: Annual Credit Plan of the State
Five Year Plan of the State
x: NABARD's district PLPs roll up into the State Focus Paper, which is the base for the State's Annual Credit Plan.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Regional Rural Banks – Principal institution for MSMEs
State Land Development Banks – Long-term agricultural loans
x: State Land Development Banks give long-term agricultural loans. NABARD mainly refinances, RRBs lend directly in rural areas and SIDBI is the principal institution for MSMEs.

s: What is the main role of the District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCB) in the short-term cooperative credit structure?
x: The DCCB is the district tier that finances PACS, which lend directly to farmers; long-term loans come from Land Development Banks.

s: Which institution is the main financing institution for MSMEs, not agriculture?
x: SIDBI is the main institution for MSMEs; NABARD and the others serve agriculture and rural credit.

s: Which of the following does NOT give direct credit to farmers?
x: NABARD only refinances other banks; PACS, RRBs and Land Development Banks lend directly.

s: In which year was the first Land Development Bank set up at Jhang?
x: The first Land Development Bank was set up at Jhang (Punjab) in 1920.

s: What are Land Development Banks now called?
o: Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks
x: Land Development Banks, the long-term arm of the cooperative structure, are now called Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks.

s: When was the first Regional Rural Bank, Prathama Grameen Bank, set up?
x: Prathama Grameen Bank began on 2 October 1975; RRBs are regulated by NABARD and supported by sponsor banks.

s:
Regional Rural Banks provide loans and advances mainly to:
1. Small and marginal farmers
2. Rural artisans
3. Large industrial borrowers
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: RRBs lend mainly to small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers and rural artisans, not to large industry.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Regional Rural Banks?
o: They do not participate in institutional agricultural credit
They provide banking services in rural and semi-urban areas
They mobilise financial resources in rural areas
x: RRBs do give institutional farm credit, so the first statement is false.

s: After the amalgamation under 'One State, One RRB' effective 1 May 2025, how many RRBs remain?
x: 26 RRBs were amalgamated in the fourth phase, leaving 28 RRBs.

s:
Consider the following statements about Regional Rural Banks:
1. They are sponsored by Scheduled Commercial Banks.
2. They are regulated by NABARD.
3. They took over the agricultural refinance functions of NABARD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: RRBs are sponsored by Scheduled Commercial Banks and regulated by NABARD; they do not take over agricultural refinance functions.

s: The Working Group on Rural Banks (1975), chaired by M. Narasimham, led to the setting up of which institutions?
x: The Narasimham Working Group (1975) recommended RRBs; the first RRBs came up on 2 October 1975.

s: In what ratio is the share capital of a Regional Rural Bank held by the Centre, the sponsor bank and the State Government?
x: The Centre holds 50%, the sponsor commercial bank 35% and the State Government 15% of an RRB's capital.

s: Where was the first Regional Rural Bank, Prathama Grameen Bank, set up?
x: Prathama Grameen Bank, the first RRB, was set up at Moradabad (UP) on 2 October 1975.

s: How many Regional Rural Banks were set up in 1975?
x: Five RRBs were set up in 1975, the first being Prathama Grameen Bank at Moradabad.

s: Which of the following sets of banks issues Kisan Credit Cards?
o: Payment banks, RRBs and cooperative banks
Commercial banks, RRBs and small finance banks
Commercial banks, local area banks and payment banks
Small finance banks, payment banks and local area banks
x: KCCs are issued by commercial banks, cooperative banks, RRBs and small finance banks; payment banks and local area banks are not issuers.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a purpose covered under the Kisan Credit Card scheme?
o: Maintenance of farm assets and allied activities
Purchase of controlling shares in commercial banks
x: KCC covers crop cultivation, post-harvest and marketing loans, household consumption, maintenance of farm assets and investment credit for allied activities. Purchase of controlling shares in banks is not a KCC purpose.

s: Under the Kisan Credit Card scheme, the collateral-free loan limit is up to ₹2 lakh, while it can rise to what amount with a hypothecation tie-up?
x: KCC loans are collateral-free up to ₹2 lakh and may extend to ₹3 lakh with a hypothecation tie-up.

s: To how many years do the RBI's revised Kisan Credit Card Directions (19 June 2026) raise the maximum KCC tenure?
x: Tenure rises to 6 years from 5, for loans from 1 January 2027.

s: In which year was the Kisan Credit Card facility extended to animal husbandry and fisheries farmers?
x: KCC was extended to animal husbandry and fisheries from 2019, with interest subvention; extension to allied and non-farm activities came in 2004.

s: Which of the following is NOT covered by short-term credit under the Kisan Credit Card scheme?
x: Short-term KCC credit does not cover purchase of combine harvesters, tractors or mini trucks; consumption and working capital are covered.

s: On whose Working Group's recommendation were electronic Kisan Credit Cards introduced?
x: Electronic KCCs follow the T.M. Bhasin Working Group; R.V. Gupta recommended the KCC itself.

s: About how many Kisan Credit Cards were operative as on 31 March 2025?
x: There were 7.72 crore operative KCCs on 31 March 2025, with ₹10.20 lakh crore outstanding.

s: The share of non-institutional sources in agricultural credit fell from about 90 per cent in 1950 to what level?
x: The non-institutional share of agricultural credit fell from about 90 per cent in 1950 to 23.4 per cent in 2021-22.

s: Which sector experienced a notable rise in credit flow following the monetary and financial reforms initiated after 1991?
x: The agricultural sector experienced a notable increase in credit flow following the monetary policy reforms introduced after 1991.

s: Ground Level Credit to agriculture in FY25 was about ₹28.69 lakh crore. What was the target?
x: FY25 Ground Level Credit was ₹28.69 lakh crore against a target of ₹27.50 lakh crore (104%); NABARD projects over ₹32.5 lakh crore for FY26.

s: About three-fourths of institutional credit to agriculture in India comes from which source?
x: Commercial banks are the largest source of agricultural credit, giving about three-fourths of it in 2021-22.

s:
Consider the following statements about institutional agricultural credit in India:
1. Commercial banks give the largest share.
2. Regional Rural Banks give more credit than cooperative banks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The order is commercial banks > cooperative banks > RRBs, so only statement 1 is correct.

s: Which region of India gets about 48 per cent of agricultural credit with only about 17 per cent of the cropped area?
x: Agricultural credit is skewed to the South (48%); the East gets only 8.2% and the Central region 13.7%.

s: Agricultural loans for more than how many years are classed as long-term credit?
x: Short-term is up to 15 months, medium-term 15 months to 5 years and long-term over 5 years.

s: Agricultural loans up to how many months are classed as short-term credit?
x: Short-term farm credit runs up to 15 months; medium-term is 15 months to 5 years.

s: Against which document are post-harvest loans at 7 per cent for up to six months available under the interest-subvention framework?
o: Equity shares of farmer producer organisations
x: Post-harvest loans are available at 7 per cent for up to six months against negotiable warehouse receipts recognised under WDRA, particularly for small and marginal farmers.

s: What does the Kisan Rin Portal, launched in September 2023, mainly integrate?
o: Kisan Credit Card data with interest-subvention claims
x: The Kisan Rin Portal integrates KCC information with interest-subvention claims.

s: Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, what is the effective interest rate on short-term KCC loans for prompt repayers?
x: Loans are at 7%; a 3% prompt repayment incentive brings the effective rate to 4%.

s: Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS), what interest subvention is given to lending institutions on short-term KCC crop loans?
x: Lenders get 1.5 per cent subvention. 3 per cent is the prompt repayment incentive to farmers, 4 per cent is the farmer's effective rate after it, and 7 per cent is the lending rate.

s: To what amount was the loan limit for interest subvention under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme raised in August 2026?
x: The MISS limit was raised to ₹5 lakh in August 2026 from the earlier Rs 3 lakh.

s: What type of scheme is the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS)?
x: MISS is a Central Sector scheme run through RBI and NABARD.

s: The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme launched by NABARD in 1992 is regarded as which of the following?
o: The first rural land development bank
x: NABARD’s SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, launched in 1992, is regarded as the world’s largest microfinance programme.

s: In which year was NABARD's SHG-Bank Linkage Programme launched?
x: The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was launched in 1992; the Kisan Credit Card dates from 1998.

s: In which year did the nationalisation of 14 banks and the introduction of the Lead Bank Scheme take place?
x: Bank nationalisation and the Lead Bank Scheme came in 1969, after the first land development bank (1920) and before RRBs (1975) and NABARD (1982).

s: NABARD was set up on the recommendation of which committee?
o: Agricultural Credit Review Committee chaired by A.M. Khusro
Working Group on Rural Banks chaired by M. Narasimham
All India Rural Credit Survey Committee chaired by A.D. Gorwala
x: NABARD was recommended by CRAFICARD (Committee to Review Arrangements for Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development, 1979-81) chaired by B. Sivaraman. Khusro chaired the 1989 Agricultural Credit Review Committee, Narasimham the 1975 Working Group on Rural Banks (RRBs), and Gorwala the 1951-54 rural credit survey.

s: The Kisan Credit Card scheme was launched in August 1998 as a model scheme of which institution, on the recommendation of which committee?
x: KCC (August 1998) is a NABARD model scheme based on the R.V. Gupta Committee. V.S. Vyas chaired the 2004 Advisory Committee on Flow of Credit to Agriculture, A.M. Khusro the 1989 Agricultural Credit Review Committee, and M. Narasimham the 1975 Working Group on Rural Banks.

s: Which of the following pairs of rural credit committees and chairmen is correctly matched?
o: All India Rural Credit Survey – A.M. Khusro
Flow of Credit to Agriculture (2004) – V.S. Vyas
Agricultural Credit Review Committee (1989) – A.D. Gorwala
x: V.S. Vyas chaired the 2004 committee on flow of credit; AIRCS was Gorwala, the 1989 review was Khusro, and CRAFICARD was B. Sivaraman.

s: Who chaired the All India Rural Credit Survey (1951-54)?
x: A.D. Gorwala chaired the All India Rural Credit Survey (1951-54).

s: Who chaired CRAFICARD?
x: CRAFICARD – B. Sivaraman; AIRCS – A.D. Gorwala; Working Group on Rural Banks – M. Narasimham; Agricultural Credit Review Committee – A.M. Khusro.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Committee)
A. Working Group on Rural Banks (1975)
B. CRAFICARD
C. R.V. Gupta Committee
D. Bhandari Committee
List-II (Outcome)
1. NABARD
2. Kisan Credit Card
3. Regional Rural Banks
4. Restructuring of RRBs
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Narasimham group gave RRBs, Sivaraman's CRAFICARD gave NABARD, R.V. Gupta gave KCC and Bhandari (1994) dealt with RRB restructuring.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Lead Bank Scheme
2. First Land Development Bank
3. Establishment of NABARD
4. Kisan Rin Portal
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: First LDB 1920, Lead Bank Scheme 1969, NABARD 1982 and Kisan Rin Portal 2023.

s: Who chaired the Agricultural Credit Review Committee (1989)?
x: The Agricultural Credit Review Committee of 1989 was headed by A.M. Khusro.

s: What is the overall priority sector lending target for Regional Rural Banks and small finance banks?
x: RRBs and SFBs face a higher PSL target of 75% of ANBC than commercial banks (40%).

s: Within the 18% agriculture PSL target, what is the sub-target for small and marginal farmers?
x: The small and marginal farmers' sub-target is 10%; 14% is the sub-target for non-corporate farmers.

s: What do Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs) allow banks to do?
o: convert farm loans into government grants
opt out of priority sector obligations
meet priority sector targets by buying certificates
insure loans given to small farmers
x: PSLCs let banks buy certificates representing priority sector lending to meet their targets; they do not remove the obligation.

s: Which of the following is NOT included among the stated priority-sector categories?
x: Priority-sector categories include agriculture, MSME, export credit, education, housing, social infrastructure and renewable energy, among others. Luxury consumer goods are not listed.

s: What narrower priority sector lending target did the Narasimham Committee (1991) propose?
x: The committee urged phasing out directed credit and a narrower PSL target of 10%.

s: The overall priority sector lending target for domestic commercial banks is what share of ANBC?
x: Domestic banks must lend 40% of ANBC to the priority sector; RRBs and SFBs face 75%.

s: What is the priority sector lending target for non-corporate farmers?
x: Non-corporate farmers have a 14% target, within the 18% agriculture target; small and marginal farmers have 10%.

s: Which of the following is a channel used in Andhra Pradesh to finance tenant farmers?
x: AP finances tenants through Joint Liability Groups, Rythu Mitra Groups and individual CCRC loans; NABARD does not lend directly to farmers and payment banks do not issue KCCs.

s:
Consider the following about Andhra Pradesh's SHG-Bank Linkage Programme:
1. Andhra Pradesh ranks first in the country.
2. It accounts for about 36 per cent of national disbursement.
3. Its recovery rate is about 97 per cent.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: AP ranks first, contributes about 36 per cent of national disbursement and records 99.99 per cent recovery, not 97 per cent.

s: Under Andhra Pradesh's Pavala Vaddi scheme, what is the subsidy on loans of ₹1-3 lakh repaid within a year?
x: Pavala Vaddi gives 1 per cent on loans of ₹1-3 lakh, while Vaddi Leni Runalu gives 4 per cent on loans up to ₹1 lakh; both cover loans repaid within a year.

s: What share of the agriculture target of Andhra Pradesh's Annual Credit Plan 2025-26 was disbursed?
x: ACP 2025-26 had an agri target of ₹3,06,000 crore; ₹2,96,764 crore (97%) was disbursed.

s: Andhra Pradesh's priority sector lending in 2025-26 was what share of ANBC?
x: AP's PSL in 2025-26 was 63.28% of ANBC, with agriculture at 42.11%.

s: With whose support are PACS in Andhra Pradesh being made Multi-Service Centres?
x: Andhra Pradesh's PACS are being turned into Multi-Service Centres with NABARD support.

s: Under Andhra Pradesh's Vaddi Leni Runalu scheme, what interest subsidy is given on loans up to ₹1 lakh repaid within a year?
x: Vaddi Leni Runalu gives a 4% subsidy on loans up to ₹1 lakh; Pavala Vaddi gives 1% on ₹1-3 lakh.

s: Under which NABARD fund was Andhra Pradesh's Indira Jala Prabha (2011) financed?
x: NABARD sanctioned about ₹399 crore for Indira Jala Prabha under RIDF-XVII, in convergence with MGNREGS.

s: What did Indira Jala Prabha, launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2011, mainly provide on the lands of SC and ST farmers?
x: Indira Jala Prabha gave irrigation (borewells) on SC and ST farmers' lands with NABARD RIDF and MGNREGS funds.

s: The proposal known as “One Nation, One Regulator” in agricultural quality certification primarily seeks to address which issue?
o: Replacement of all State mandis by private markets
Transfer of procurement from FCI to SFAC
Ending dual certification under BIS and AGMARK
x: The proposal seeks to end the dual certification arrangement involving BIS and AGMARK through a single regulatory framework.

s: AGMARK, the quality certification mark for agricultural produce, is issued under which Act?
o: Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956
x: AGMARK is issued under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937. 'Grading and Marketing' is a common misprint used as a trap. The BIS Act governs BIS certification, and the 1956 Act set up the CWC.

s: Where are the Central Agmark Laboratory and the Central Quality Control Laboratory located?
x: Both the Central Agmark Laboratory (APPSC 2018 key) and the Central Quality Control Laboratory (APPSC 2025 key) are at Nagpur. New Delhi, Faridabad and Hyderabad are distractors.

s: AGMARK certification is administered by which organisation?
x: AGMARK certification is administered by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI) under the Ministry of Agriculture.

s: What is AGMARKNET, launched in 2000?
o: A portal for agricultural market prices
A quality mark for farm produce
A registry of contract farming agreements
x: AGMARKNET (2000, NIC) is a price portal for agricultural markets, now Agmarknet 2.0.

s: Which of the following is NOT a reform required from States for participation in e-NAM?
o: A single licence valid across the State
Regulating all agricultural prices through the State Government
A single-point levy of market fee
x: The required reforms include a single State-wide licence, single-point market-fee levy and electronic trading. State-wide administrative price regulation is not the specified reform.

s:
Consider the following about e-NAM:
1. It is a virtual market backed by physical APMC mandis.
2. It replaces all physical mandis.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: e-NAM is a virtual market that networks existing physical APMC mandis; it does not replace them.

s: Which of the following e-NAM modules enables the sale of produce stored in WDRA-regulated warehouses?
x: Warehouse trading with electronic negotiable warehouse receipts (e-NWRs) enables produce stored in WDRA warehouses to be sold through e-NAM.

s: In 2024-25, how many mandis in Andhra Pradesh participated in inter-mandi trade on e-NAM?
x: Only 11 mandis participated in inter-mandi trade, and online payments were just ₹26.88 lakh.

s: How many markets in Andhra Pradesh are integrated with e-NAM?
x: AP has 33 e-NAM markets trading dry chillies, cotton, turmeric, groundnut and more.

s: Under e-NAM, to whom is payment for produce made directly?
x: e-NAM enables direct payment to farmers' accounts, besides transparent price discovery and wider buyer access.

s: Through which fund has e-NAM, a Central Sector Scheme, been funded?
x: e-NAM is funded via the Agri-Tech Infrastructure Fund and now falls under ISAM-eNAM.

s: About how many mandis were integrated with e-NAM as of March 2026?
x: By March 2026 e-NAM covered 1,656 mandis in 23 States and 4 UTs.

s: Which slogan is associated with e-NAM?
x: e-NAM, launched in April 2016, works on the idea of 'One Nation, One Market'.

s: Up to how much assistance is given per mandi for joining e-NAM?
x: Each mandi joining e-NAM can get up to ₹75 lakh.

s: e-NAM was launched in which month and year?
x: The National Agriculture Market, or e-NAM, was launched in April 2016.

s: Which organisation is the lead implementing agency for e-NAM?
o: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority
National Agriculture Cooperative Marketing Federation of India
x: The Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) is the lead implementing agency for e-NAM.

s: What is the first step in establishing a regulated market in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Notification of the area by the Government
The yard coming under the committee's operation
x: The order is: Government notifies the area, the Market Committee is constituted, the yard is set up and then operated by the committee.

s: Agricultural markets are regulated by APMC Acts of the States because they fall in which list?
x: Agricultural markets are a State subject; hence APMC laws are enacted by State legislatures.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature ensured by regulated agricultural markets?
o: Compulsory sale exclusively to unlicensed buyers
x: Regulated markets provide open auctions, standard weights, recorded prices and licensed buyers; they do not require sale to unlicensed buyers.

s: What is the market fee levied in regulated agricultural markets?
x: The market fee is 1%; AP AMCs collected ₹429.77 crore in 2025-26 (to December 2025).

s: In which year was the AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, which still governs agricultural markets in Andhra Pradesh, enacted?
x: The AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966 (Act 16 of 1966) remains the operative framework.

s: About how many regulated agricultural markets are there in India?
x: India has about 2,477 regulated markets and 4,843 sub-yards.

s: Which one of the following is a problem associated with the APMC system?
o: Excessive number of mandis in every locality
Absence of any market fee or commission charge
Cartels of licensed traders and dependence on approved middlemen
x: Cartels of licensed traders, market and licence fees, commission charges, too few mandis and dependence on approved middlemen are identified problems.

s: How is price spread in agricultural marketing calculated?
x: Price spread is the consumer price minus the price received by the farmer; it indicates marketing margins and the share of intermediaries.

s: The National Commission on Farmers suggested that a regulated market should be available within approximately what distance of farmers?
x: The National Commission on Farmers suggested a regulated market within about 5 km of farmers.

s: With about 40% of storage lying idle, what does poor storage in agricultural marketing mainly lead to?
x: Poor storage (~40% idle) forces farmers into distress sale.

s: According to RBI studies (October 2024), what is the farmer's share in the consumer rupee for tomato?
x: Tomato farmers get about 33% of the consumer rupee, onion ~36% and potato ~37%.

s:
Consider the following statements about the farmer's share in the consumer rupee:
1. Farmers get a higher share for pulses than for perishables.
2. Gram gives farmers about 75% of the consumer rupee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Pulses give farmers a higher share (gram ~75%, moong ~70%, tur ~65%) than perishables such as tomato (~33%).

s: Which one of the following was a feature of the Model APMC Act, 2003?
o: Whole State treated as one market area
Livestock and services brought within contract farming regulation
Contract farming kept outside the APMC framework
x: The Model APMC Act, 2003 permitted direct sale of agricultural produce to contract-farming sponsors. The other features are associated with the 2017 or 2018 model acts.

s: What did the Model APLM Act, 2017 propose?
o: keeping contract farming outside the APMC purview
treating the entire State as one market area
transfer of land title to the contract sponsor
x: The Model APLM Act, 2017 proposed treating the whole State as one market area; keeping contract farming outside APMC belongs to the 2018 Contract Farming Act.

s: Under the Model Contract Farming Act, 2018, how much of the produce must the sponsor purchase?
o: Only a part of the pre-agreed quantity
At least half of the pre-agreed quantity
Only produce that meets export grades
x: The sponsor must buy the entire pre-agreed quantity and gets no right in the farmer's land.

s: The Model Contract Farming Act, 2018 treats which party as the weaker party?
x: The model Act recognises the farmer as the weaker party and keeps contract farming outside the APMC Act.

s: Under the Model Contract Farming Act, 2018, which body registers agreements online?
x: Registration is by the RARC; CFFGs work at village/panchayat level.

s: In which year did the AP Markets (Amendment) Act add contract farming to Andhra Pradesh's markets law?
x: The AP Markets (Amendment) Act, 2005 added contract farming (Section 11A); sponsors register with the Registering Authority.

s: The Agricultural Produce and Livestock Markets in Andhra Pradesh are governed by which enactment?
o: Andhra Pradesh Agricultural Marketing and Warehousing Act, 1966
AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966
x: The governing law is the AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966.

s: Under the Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act, 2020, how was trade in a 'trade area' outside APMC yards treated?
o: Subject to the State market fee
x: Trade-area transactions were outside APMC yards and free of State market fee; the Act did not mention MSP.

s: Which 2020 law removed stock limits on cereals, pulses, oilseeds, edible oils, onion and potato except in extraordinary situations?
o: Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act
Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act
x: The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020 removed these stock limits; contract farming was the subject of the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement Act.

s: When were the 2020 farm laws repealed?
x: The laws were repealed in November 2021; the AP Markets Act, 1966 remains the operative framework.

s: The 2020 farm laws were enacted by Parliament by invoking which constitutional legislative entry, although agriculture is primarily in the State List?
x: The laws were enacted by invoking Concurrent List Entry 33, while agriculture is associated with State List Entry 14.

s: Which of the 2020 farm laws did not mention MSP while allowing trade outside APMC yards?
o: Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act
Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act
x: The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act allowed trade in a 'trade area' without State fee but did not mention MSP.

s: The e-Choupal initiative is associated with which organisation?
x: e-Choupal consists of ITC’s Internet kiosks linking farmers with markets.

s: In contract farming, on what do farmers agree in advance with an agri-business firm?
o: Transfer of ownership of their land
Price, quantity and/or time of sale
Sale only through APMC market yards
Permanent structures on their land for the firm
x: In contract farming, the farmer and the firm agree in advance on the price, quantity and/or time of sale. There is no transfer of the farmer's land.

s: On what is the 'Small Farmer Large Field' model based?
o: Dividing large farms into individual plots for subsistence cultivation
Leasing all farmland to a single corporate sponsor
Pooling neighbouring small farmers’ holdings for joint operation as one large field
Compulsory consolidation of all landholdings by the State
x: Under this model, neighbouring small farmers pool their holdings and operate them as one large field to obtain scale in inputs and marketing.

s: Which State is identified as the pioneer of contract farming, associated with PepsiCo in the late 1980s?
x: Punjab is identified as the pioneer of contract farming in this context, with PepsiCo in the late 1980s.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs?
o: It was launched in 2020 with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore
Management support of ₹18 lakh per FPO is spread over three years
Handholding through CBBOs is given to each FPO for three years
x: Handholding through CBBOs lasts five years; it is the ₹18 lakh management support that is spread over three years.

s: Which implementing agency of the 10,000 FPO scheme also promotes cooperative-sector FPOs through the PACS route?
x: NCDC, one of the implementing agencies with SFAC, NABARD and NAFED, promotes cooperative FPOs through PACS.

s: At what level does the 10,000 FPO scheme envisage one FPO?
x: The norm is one FPO per block, not per district; 15% of FPOs are to be in Aspirational Districts.

s: Under the 10,000 FPO scheme, the equity grant is up to how much per farmer member?
x: The equity grant is Rs 2,000 per member, capped at Rs 15 lakh per FPO; credit guarantee is up to Rs 2 crore.

s: Which of the following is NOT a rationale of the 10,000 FPO scheme?
x: The scheme aims at bargaining power, scale economies and lower costs; it does not transfer land to FPOs.

s: What is NAFED?
o: Central agency for food-grain storage alone
x: NAFED is the apex agricultural cooperative marketing body and was set up in 1958.

s: Which crops are procured at MSP under the Price Support Scheme of PM-AASHA?
x: The Price Support Scheme procures pulses, oilseeds and copra at MSP.

s: With which of the following is TRIFED mainly associated?
o: Price support for oilseeds and copra
x: TRIFED is concerned with marketing tribal produce. It was established in 1987 under the framework associated with the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 1984.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: AP MARKFED – ₹3,000 crore Price Stabilisation Fund
NCCF – Accreditation of warehouses under WDRA
x: NCCF has nothing to do with WDRA accreditation, which is done by WDRA itself; the other pairs are correct.

s: Up to what amount is credit guarantee cover available under the 10,000 FPO scheme?
x: The scheme gives credit guarantee up to ₹2 crore; equity grant is ₹2,000 per member with a ₹15 lakh cap.

s: Which body in Andhra Pradesh holds a ₹3,000 crore Price Stabilisation Fund?
x: AP MARKFED, the State cooperative marketing federation, holds a ₹3,000 crore Price Stabilisation Fund.

s: In which year was NAFED, the apex cooperative marketing body, set up?
x: NAFED was set up on 2 October 1958 as the national apex cooperative marketing body.

s: In which year was TRIFED set up?
x: TRIFED, for marketing tribal produce, was set up in 1987; NAFED dates from 1958.

s: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), launched in 2020, provides a medium- and long-term debt-financing facility of what amount for post-harvest infrastructure and community farming assets?
x: The AIF is a ₹1 lakh crore medium- and long-term debt-financing facility launched in 2020 for post-harvest infrastructure and community farming assets.

s: Which Ministry implements Operation Greens?
x: Operation Greens, modelled on Operation Flood and begun with TOP crops, is run by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Operation Greens?
o: Its extension to 22 perishable crops was announced in the Union Budget 2018-19
The 2020 Atmanirbhar Bharat package extended it to all fruits and vegetables
The Union Budget 2021-22 extended it to 22 perishable crops
It was announced for TOP crops in the Union Budget 2018-19
x: Budget 2018-19 announced Operation Greens for TOP; the 22-crop extension came in Budget 2021-22.

s: Under Operation Greens, how much grant-in-aid do long-term value-chain projects of FPOs get?
x: FPOs get 70% grant-in-aid (50% for others); short-term interventions get 50% subsidy on transport and storage.

s: Which of the following was announced in the Union Budget 2018-19 to address the price volatility of tomato, onion and potato?
x: Operation Greens was announced in the Union Budget 2018-19 for TOP crops (APPSC 2018 key). Operation Flood is the dairy programme it is modelled on, Mission Indradhanush is an immunisation mission, and SAMPADA is a food-processing scheme.

s: Up to what loan amount does the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund provide 3% interest subvention?
x: AIF gives 3% subvention on loans up to ₹2 crore, with credit guarantee through CGTMSE.

s: Operation Greens was extended from TOP to TOTAL in Budget 2021-22 to cover how many perishables?
x: TOP to TOTAL (Budget 2021-22) extended Operation Greens to 22 perishables.

s: Through which body is credit guarantee given for loans under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund?
x: AIF loans up to ₹2 crore get credit guarantee through CGTMSE.

s: Who runs Rythu Bazars in Andhra Pradesh?
o: An Estate Officer under the Revenue Department
x: An Estate Officer under the Revenue Department runs Rythu Bazars, outside the Agricultural Market Committees.

s:
Consider the following about Rythu Bazars in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Farmers sell produce directly to consumers.
2. They avoid commission agents.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: Rythu Bazars enable direct sale by farmers to consumers, avoiding commission agents.

s: The Union Budget 2018-19 proposed upgrading how many rural haats into Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs)?
x: The Union Budget 2018-19 announced upgrading 22,000 rural haats, not 10,000, into GrAMs.

s: Which of the following farmers' markets is correctly matched with its State?
x: Hadapsar Mandi is in Pune, Maharashtra. Rythu Bazar is Andhra Pradesh, Uzhavar Sandhai Tamil Nadu and Apni Mandi Punjab.

s: In which Union Budget were Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs) proposed?
x: GrAMs were announced in Budget 2018-19, to be exempt from APMC regulation and linked to e-NAM.

s: Krishi UDAN Yojana primarily seeks to achieve which of the following?
o: Transport farm produce, particularly perishables, by air to improve farmers’ prices and incomes
Establish permanent wholesale mandis in every district
Replace agricultural markets with electronic warehouses
Provide free crop insurance to farmers in drought-prone areas
x: Krishi UDAN facilitates air transport of agricultural produce, especially perishables, helping farmers obtain better prices and higher incomes.

s: Uzhavar Sandhai, a farmers' direct market, belongs to which State?
x: Uzhavar Sandhai is Tamil Nadu's; Rythu Bazar is AP's, Apni Mandi Punjab's and Hadapsar Mandi Maharashtra's.

s: In which year did Rythu Bazars, Andhra Pradesh's direct farmer-consumer markets, begin?
x: AP's first direct farmer-consumer market, the Rythu Bazar, began in 1999.

s: About how many Rythu Bazars were functional in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26?
x: Andhra Pradesh had 129 functional Rythu Bazars in 2025-26.

s: What is the size of the Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund set up for Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs)?
x: A ₹2,000 crore Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund supports the upgrading of rural haats into GrAMs.

s: On which platform are Electronic Negotiable Warehouse Receipts (e-NWRs) tradable?
x: e-NWRs are tradable on e-NAM and can also support pledge finance.

s: Under which Act was the Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) set up on 2 March 1957?
o: Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956
x: CWC was established on 2 March 1957 under the Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956. It is now associated with the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962.

s: The 'World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector', piloted in 2023, is under which Ministry, and at what level are its godowns built?
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; FCI depot level
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; district level
Ministry of Food Processing Industries; mega food park level
x: The plan belongs to the Ministry of Cooperation (piloted 2023) and builds godowns and processing units at the PACS level, with NCDC implementing it alongside NABARD, CWC and FCI. The other ministries and levels are distractors.

s:
Assertion (A): The World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector is implemented by NCDC with NABARD, CWC and FCI.
Reason (R): Under the plan, the effective interest rate for PACS works out to 3%.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is correct, but 3% is the AIF interest subvention; with NABARD refinance the effective rate for PACS falls to 1%.

s: In which year was the Warehousing (Development and Regulation) Act enacted?
x: The WDR Act is of 2007, in force from 25 October 2010; WDRA was set up on 26 October 2010.

s: Which body accredits warehouses and negotiable warehouse receipts in India?
x: The Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA), set up on 26 October 2010, accredits warehouses and NWRs.

s: e-Kisan Upaj Nidhi, launched on 4 March 2024, is linked with which regulator?
x: e-Kisan Upaj Nidhi is a WDRA initiative for loans against electronic negotiable warehouse receipts.

s: In which year was the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA) set up?
x: WDRA was set up on 26 October 2010; the Act was passed in 2007.

s: If the market price of an MSP-covered crop falls below the announced MSP, which of the following normally occurs under the MSP mechanism?
o: The Reserve Bank of India purchases the stock through open-market operations
Government agencies purchase the stock offered by farmers
The MSP is automatically cancelled for that season
Farmers are prohibited from selling the crop in the market
x: When the market price falls below MSP, government agencies procure the stock offered, providing a safeguard against distress sales.

s: What does Minimum Support Price (MSP) mean?
o: Minimum export price fixed by farmers
Government-announced minimum price for selected agricultural commodities
Market-determined maximum price for all agricultural commodities
x: MSP is the minimum price the government announces for selected farm crops, at which it will buy if market prices fall below it.

s:
Consider the following about MSP:
1. It is fixed by the CACP.
2. It protects farmers against a sharp fall in market prices.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: MSP protects farmers against price falls, but it is fixed by the Government of India (CCEA); the CACP only recommends it.

s: Who finally fixes the Minimum Support Price?
x: The CACP recommends MSP, and the Government of India fixes it.

s: Which of the following is true of the Minimum Support Price in India?
o: A statutory entitlement under an MSP law
An administrative decision not backed by a statute
x: MSP is an administrative decision announced before sowing; it is not backed by a statute.

s: In which year was the Agricultural Prices Commission renamed the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)?
x: The APC was set up in 1965 and renamed CACP in 1985.

s: What is the status of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)?
o: A statutory body under an Act of Parliament
An attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
An attached office of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs
x: CACP is an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; it is not a statutory body.

s: Besides the Chairman, who are the members of the CACP?
o: A Member Secretary and four official members
Two official and two non-official members
A Member Secretary, one official member and two non-official members
A Member Secretary, two official members and one non-official member
x: The CACP has a Chairman, a Member Secretary, one official member and two non-official members.

s: For which programme does MSP-based procurement mainly build food stocks?
x: MSP procurement builds the grain stocks used for the Public Distribution System, which links it to food security.

s: Which of the following commercial crops is covered under MSP?
x: Raw jute, along with cotton and copra, is a commercial crop under MSP.

s: Which of the following is a cash crop?
x: Tobacco, like cotton, sugarcane and oilseeds, is a cash crop grown mainly for sale; rice, millets and pulses are subsistence crops.

s: How are the 22 mandated MSP crops classified by the CACP?
x: The stated split is 14 kharif crops, 6 rabi crops and 2 commercial crops, totalling 22 mandated crops.

s: How many crops are covered under MSP in all?
x: MSP covers 22 crops: 7 cereals, 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds and 3 commercial crops.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Gram is a pulse. Paddy is a cereal, groundnut an oilseed and copra a commercial crop.

s: Which agency is the nodal agency for MSP operations relating to cotton?
o: Food Corporation of India under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs
National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation under the Ministry of Finance
Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices under the Ministry of Commerce
Cotton Corporation of India under the Ministry of Textiles
x: The Cotton Corporation of India, under the Ministry of Textiles, is the nodal agency for cotton MSP operations.

s: Niger seed has an MSP and its oil is used for cooking by some tribal communities. What type of crop is it?
x: Niger seed is a Kharif crop covered under MSP.

s: Which of the following crops has no Minimum Support Price?
x: Turmeric, areca nut and coffee have no MSP; ragi, nigerseed and safflower are among the 22 mandated crops.

s: How many oilseeds are covered under Minimum Support Price?
x: Seven oilseeds have MSP: groundnut, rapeseed-mustard, soybean, sunflower, sesamum, safflower and nigerseed.

s: Which crop got the largest MSP hike for Kharif 2026-27?
x: Sunflower recorded the largest hike, increasing by ₹622 per quintal. The increases for cotton, niger seed and common paddy were ₹557, ₹515 and ₹72 respectively.

s: What is the MSP for wheat for Rabi Marketing Season 2026-27?
x: Wheat MSP for RMS 2026-27 is ₹2,585 per quintal, up ₹160 from ₹2,425 in 2025-26.

s: What is the MSP for common paddy for Kharif 2026-27?
x: Common paddy MSP for 2026-27 is ₹2,441 per quintal (up ₹72); ₹2,461 is Grade A and ₹2,369 was the 2025-26 MSP.

s: Which kharif crop has the highest MSP for 2026-27?
x: Sesamum has the highest MSP at ₹10,346 per quintal; sunflower got the biggest hike (₹622).

s: Besides the 22 mandated MSP crops, which crop receives a Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP)?
x: Sugarcane receives FRP in addition to the 22 mandated MSP crops, making 23 in all; jute, copra and cotton are among the 22.

s: With which of the following is the Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) mainly associated?
o: Industrial raw materials procured by the CCI
Perishable commodities not covered under MSP
Only wheat and paddy under open-ended procurement
x: MIS provides price support for perishable commodities that are not covered under MSP.

s: Which agencies undertake physical procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra at MSP under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) of PM-AASHA?
x: NAFED and NCCF are the central nodal agencies that procure pulses, oilseeds and copra under PSS at a State's request. FCI handles wheat and paddy and CCI handles cotton; the warehousing corporations store produce; SFAC and NABARD promote FPOs.

s: Which PM-AASHA component was the 2018 pilot in which private agencies procured oilseeds at MSP?
x: PPSS was the 2018 private-procurement pilot; PSS involves physical procurement by government agencies and PDPS only pays the price deficiency.

s: What minimum price fall can trigger action under the Market Intervention Scheme?
x: MIS can be triggered by a price fall of 10% or more, or a production rise of 10% or more.

s: For which pulses does the pulses mission promise 100% procurement at MSP for four years?
x: The pulses mission promises 100% procurement at MSP for four years for tur, urad and masoor through NAFED and NCCF under PSS.

s: Why was the Price Stabilisation Fund set up in 2014-15?
o: Provide unlimited procurement of all MSP crops
Finance sugar mills’ purchase of cane at SAP
Create buffers of onion, potato and pulses and release them during price spikes
Guarantee exports of wheat and paddy
x: The Price Stabilisation Fund was set up in 2014–15 to hold buffers of onion, potato and pulses and release them to curb sharp price increases.

s: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) was launched in which month and year?
x: PM-AASHA was launched in September 2018 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

s: A farmer sells an oilseed in the market below its MSP, but no physical procurement takes place. Under which PM-AASHA component may the farmer receive the difference between MSP and the market price in cash?
x: The Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS) makes a cash payment equal to the gap between MSP and the market price, mainly for oilseeds, without physical purchase.

s: In what ratio are losses under the Market Intervention Scheme shared between the Centre and North-Eastern States?
x: NE States share MIS losses 75:25; other States ordinarily share them 50:50.

s: What is the outlay for the extension of PM-AASHA up to 2025-26?
x: The outlay for the Fifteenth Finance Commission cycle up to 2025-26 is ₹35,000 crore.

s: What is the main purpose of PM-AASHA?
o: the benefits of MSP reach farmers, including small and marginal farmers
all agricultural produce is procured by private agencies
agricultural exports are completely exempt from taxation
fertiliser subsidies reach only large farmers
x: PM-AASHA seeks to make MSP reach farmers, including small and marginal farmers.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM-AASHA?
o: Under PDPS, agencies physically procure the produce
Under PSS, NAFED and NCCF procure pulses and oilseeds
x: PDPS pays the gap between MSP and market price without buying any produce; physical procurement happens under PSS.

s: In November 2020, Kerala fixed floor prices for how many vegetables?
x: Kerala became the first State to fix floor prices for 16 vegetables in November 2020.

s: What is the full form of PM-AASHA?
o: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan
Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sahayata Abhiyan
Pradhan Mantri Anna Aadhar Suraksha Abhiyan
Pradhan Mantri Annadata Ayushman Sahayata Abhiyan
x: PM-AASHA stands for Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan, launched in September 2018.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Sugarcane is covered under the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP).
The CCEA approves the FRP for sugarcane.
The CACP approves the FRP for sugarcane.
x: The CCEA, not the CACP, approves the FRP; the CACP only recommends prices.

s: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane is notified under which legal framework?
o: Sugarcane Regulation Act, 1955 under the Agricultural Produce Markets Act
Essential Commodities (Sugarcane Pricing) Rules, 1966 under the Food Corporation of India Act
Sugarcane Development Act, 2009 under the National Food Security Act
Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966 under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955
x: FRP is fixed under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

s: Who announces the State Advised Price (SAP) of sugarcane?
x: SAP is announced by certain States such as UP, Punjab and Haryana, usually above FRP; it is not fixed by the CACP.

s: Who fixes the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane?
o: The CCEA on the CACP's recommendation
x: FRP is fixed by the CCEA on CACP's recommendation and linked to the mill's recovery rate; the State-announced price is SAP.

s: From which year was the Statutory Minimum Price (SMP) of sugarcane replaced by the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP)?
x: FRP replaced SMP from 2009-10, after the Sugarcane (Control) Order was amended on 22.10.2009.

s: To which factor is the Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane linked?
x: FRP is the minimum price mills must pay and is linked to the sugar recovery rate.

s: Who mainly procures coarse grains for the Central Pool?
o: State agencies with prior approval of the Government of India
The Reserve Bank of India after approval of the CACP
Only the Cotton Corporation of India
District cooperative banks without central approval
x: State agencies procure coarse grains for the Central Pool, but prior approval of the Government of India is required.

s: Which of the following crops is procured at MSP on an effectively open-ended basis?
x: FCI and State agencies buy all wheat and paddy meeting specifications; pulses and oilseeds get limited PSS procurement.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about procurement at MSP?
o: Pulses, oilseeds and copra are procured under PSS with a 25% cap
Cotton is procured through the Cotton Corporation of India
Coarse grains are procured exclusively by the FCI
Wheat and paddy procurement is effectively open-ended
x: Coarse grains are procured by State agencies, not exclusively by the FCI; the other three statements are correct.

s: In which year was Decentralised Procurement (DCP) of foodgrains introduced?
x: DCP began in 1997; States procure, store and distribute, and the Centre reimburses economic cost minus CIP.

s: Through which bodies is paddy mainly bought from farmers at MSP in Andhra Pradesh?
x: DCMS societies procure paddy at MSP in Andhra Pradesh, with APMARKFED as the apex cooperative marketing body.

s: In which year was Bt cotton approved for commercial cultivation in India?
x: Bt cotton, a GM crop, was approved for commercial cultivation in India in 2002.

s: Which of the following pairs (phase – hallmark) is wrongly matched?
o: Green Revolution phase – HYV wheat and rice
Post-1991 phase – direct income support through PM-KISAN
Price-support and procurement phase – PDS distribution at issue price
x: WTO membership came in the post-1991 period, not the Pre-Green Revolution phase.

s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, the de minimis limit on amber-box support for developing countries is what share of production value?
x: Developing countries may give amber-box support up to 10% of production value; the limit for developed countries is 5%.

s: At which WTO meeting was the 'peace clause' protecting public stockholding for food security agreed?
x: The peace clause agreed at Bali in 2013 protects public stockholding programmes for food security.

s: Which of the following is a hallmark of the post-1991 phase of Indian agricultural development?
o: Setting up of the APC and FCI
x: The post-1991 phase brought liberalisation, WTO (1995), e-NAM, FPOs and PM-KISAN; HYVs and APC/FCI belong to the Green Revolution phase.

s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, which box covers support such as research and infrastructure that is not subject to limits?
x: Green box support (research, infrastructure) is unlimited; amber box is trade-distorting and capped.

s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of the WTO Agreement on Agriculture?
x: The three pillars of the Agreement on Agriculture are market access, domestic support and export subsidies.

s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, which box covers production-limiting payments?
x: Blue box covers production-limiting payments; green box covers research and infrastructure; amber box covers trade-distorting support.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the factors considered by the CACP?
o: It considers the cost of production
It considers only domestic prices, not international prices
It considers terms of trade between agriculture and non-agriculture
